- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +5+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; apply downward correction of 1-3% in next 5-7 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3-5 consecutive days below 70 or above 80), model often fails to adjust; apply smoothing or lagged correction to avoid overreacting.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic when sentiment is mixed or neutral; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-14 days to anchor forecast.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment followed by a rebound, model often misses the rebound; anticipate 1-2 days of lagged recovery and adjust forecast upward early.
